deities: Shiva (as Bhairava, depicted suckling at her breast)

history.period: Ancient/medieval (exact construction date not documented; terracotta chala-style present structure is medieval-era)
history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas and a Siddha Peeth: the third eye (some traditions say the eyeball) of Sati is believed to have fallen here when Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra dismembered her body. Sage Vashistha is said to have worshipped Tara here — legend says on the Buddha's guidance, after 300,000 recitations she appeared as a mother suckling Shiva — and the stone idol preserves that maternal form, camouflaged by a 3-ft metal image of Tara in fierce four-armed aspect with skull garland. The 19th-century mystic saint Bamakhepa (1837–1911) made it a celebrated centre of Tantric worship; the adjoining maha-shmashan cremation ground is among the most revered tantric sites in Shaktism. Daily goat sacrifice and non-veg bhog (mutton, shol maach) are part of its Tantric tradition. Date/dynasty of the present structure are undocumented — one travel source says 13th century; 19th-century development under Bamandas Mukherjee — flag.

name: Tarapith Temple
town_description: Tarapith is a temple town in the Rampurhat-II block of Birbhum district, West Bengal, on the north-flowing Dwaraka river, about 7–8 km from Rampurhat. Its economy revolves around the Tara temple, which draws ~12,000 devotees daily (~7 million a year), plus the famous cremation-ground tantric tradition.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~264–300 km)
travel.road: ~264 km from Kolkata via state highways; Tarapith Bus Stop at the town

visitor_information.best_time: October–March (Navratri and Kaushiki Amavasya see the largest crowds)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Most sources: 6:00 AM–9:00 PM daily (some list 4:00 or 5:00 AM opening; one temple-priest listing shows 6 AM–12 PM & 2–10 PM — verify)
